name: Gokaldas Exports Ltd
title: Gokaldas Exports Ltd - 532630 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Management says tariff shock is behind them and guides FY27 margins up a couple of points, but capacity adds are small (~INR300-odd crore each at steady state) and working capital rose ~INR200 crore, so the supply-side read is neutral-to-positive.

capex.peers_comment: Management said Southeast Asian and Chinese players are sitting on under-capacity utilisation and are willing to absorb cost increases.
capex.quote: many of them are sitting on under-capacity utilization

summary.headline: Gokaldas Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to about 12% (16% ex-tariff impact per management), with FY27 guided to a couple of points of margin improvement.
summary.overview: FY26 was disrupted by US reciprocal tariffs that stayed near 50% for much of the year, with AGOA lapse hitting Africa, yet total income rose 4% to INR4,065 crores and the EBITDA margin was held at the prior-year level. Q4 standalone margins improved on volume-driven operating leverage and the post-February normalisation of the penal tariff, with no tariff refunds booked. Management guides to a Y-o-Y margin improvement of a couple of percentage points in FY27 and Africa revenue of about $115-120 million, while BTPL is being merged in and is expected to turn EBITDA positive in H2 FY27. Net debt rose by INR395 crores on capex, BTPL investment and working capital, and management targets a INR75-100 crore working capital reduction in Gokaldas and Atraco.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone operating EBITDA margin Q4 FY26
financial_highlights.value: about 12% (about 16% adding back tariff impact; about 15.5% excluding provision reversals)
financial_highlights.change: Improved Q-o-Q and Y-o-Y, per analyst read of 200-400 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Net discount to customers FY26 (tariff offset)

segments.name: India operations (Gokaldas standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 operations grew 2% Y-o-Y while Indian apparel exports fell 10%; FY26 India operations grew 10% Y-o-Y. Standalone volume was 10.19 million pieces in Q4 (8.6 million ex-Matrix at INR773 realisation) and 33.627 million pieces for FY26 at INR765.

segments.name: Africa (Atraco)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about $80 million; FY27 target $115-120 million, with H1 run-rate about $24-25 million per quarter. Q4 volume 5.63 million pieces at INR405; FY26 16.27 million pieces at INR420. Management expects H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10%.

segments.name: BTPL (Bombay Rayon, fabric)
segments.commentary: Merger initiated subject to NCLT approval, expected in Q3 FY27. Utilisation near 50 lakh meters/month against 70 lakh capacity, expandable to 100 lakh for INR50-60 crores capex. FY27 revenue guided above INR1,000 crores; EBITDA breakeven in H1 and about 6-7% in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Matrix and other Indian subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Had minor setbacks in Q4 as customers shifted business to other regions during the 50% tariff period; management expects reversal in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone Y-o-Y EBITDA margin improvement of a couple of percentage points, conditional on no new tariff disruption; H1 FY27 margins still absorb about 3% sharper pricing given on H1 orders.
Africa FY27 revenue target $115-120 million (worst case $115 million), with H2 FY27 Africa EBITDA margin of 8-10%.
Working capital to be reduced by INR75-100 crores in FY27 across Gokaldas and Atraco, excluding BTPL merger impact.
Medium-term (FY28 steady state, excluding new capacity drag): India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, India:Africa revenue split about 75:25 to 80:20; BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.
Management said FY27 revenue growth would be much more than 10-12% excluding U.K./EU FTA benefits, which are not factored in; it targets at least 15% growth.
Two new premium customers in India (one US, one European) and two in Africa (one US, one European) to contribute revenue from FY27, about 5% of revenue in year one.
capex_capacity: Africa capacity expansion completed in FY26; one factory running 2 shifts on 20-25% of its capacity, with a second-shift opportunity without major capex.

Karnataka (Kolar Gold Fields) half-factory ramp-up expected through Q1-Q2 FY27 to full utilisation; Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) 1,000-machine unit expected at full utilisation by Q3 FY27 (Sept-Oct), adding about INR175 crores revenue at full capacity; Karnataka adds about INR125 crores at steady state.
Two further planned factories (about INR300 crores steady-state revenue) with capex of INR80-100 crores over two years; decision expected in the next quarter or so, with revenue mainly FY28.
Total capacity to reach 104 million pieces including 12 million added (India about 7.5 million, Africa about 4.5 million); India 52 million and Africa 40 million pieces currently, per management.
BTPL: 70 lakh meters/month capacity, expandable to 100 lakh with INR50-60 crores capex; captive fabric consumption by Gokaldas about 30-35%.
demand_pricing: Reciprocal tariff of about 50% (including penal 25%) on India until mid-February 2026; penal tariff withdrawn, then a 10% tariff applied until July 24, 2026. Section 301 tariffs may reset to about 20% for rest of world from late July; Africa not under Section 301 probe (Kenya stays at 10%).
Tariff rebates given during the penal regime were up to about 15% of order value, partly clawed back from the supply chain; sharper pricing of about 3% continues in H1 FY27 and is removed in H2.
AGOA extended to December 2026; US administration reportedly moving to country-by-country deals; Kenya FTA not expected by end-2026.
US retail sales grew 8% and UK 6% in CY25; US retailers pared imports from H2 CY25. Spring 27 orders being booked; customers ordering conservatively.

Input cost inflation from Middle East war (polyester, packaging, fuel, trims, cotton); pass-through being attempted in H2 orders, with partial recovery expected given customer resistance and competitor under-utilisation in SE Asia and China.
Hedging: about 80% of revenue hedged for the next two quarters at INR87-91/USD; 50% for the following two. Rupee depreciation benefit not yet in numbers, expected in H2.
Labour cost inflation in India: Haryana announced 35% wage increase from April 1 and UP 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 12% standalone margin be sustained, and what is the Africa margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Africa H2 FY27 EBITDA margin of 8-10% and operating leverage in India; Matrix and other subsidiaries were hit by pivoted orders in Q4 and should recover in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital reduce in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a reduction of INR75-100 crores in Gokaldas and Atraco, with BTPL's working capital to be added on merger; the INR200 crore increase reflected inventory build for Q1 orders (Chinese holidays) and year-end receivables.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to volumes if AGOA lapses again?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it refused to share AGOA-related discounts last time and let volume fall; now it has a broader Africa customer base and can offer some AGOA-related support if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Were tariff refunds booked in Q4 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: No tariff reversals were factored in; the Q4 gain came from volume-driven operating leverage and no tariff discounts after mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 margin outlook with BTPL included?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady-state FY28 India EBITDA margin 13-13.5%, Africa 10-10.5%, BTPL about 12% in FY28 and 14% in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Are the acquired entities meeting internal targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not in FY26 due to tariff disruption; management expects them to perform to plan in FY27.

risks_watch: Section 301 tariff reset from July 24, 2026 and whether India returns to about 20%.
AGOA expiry in December 2026 and timing of renewal; Kenya FTA uncertainty.
Cotton, polyester and fuel cost pass-through versus customer resistance in H2 FY27.
BTPL NCLT merger timing (Q3 FY27) and its loss-making run-rate (-4 to -5% EBITDA in Q4 FY26); integration working capital.
Labour cost inflation in North India (Haryana 35%, UP 25% wage increases).
Rupee hedges at INR87-91/USD could limit currency gains; debt rising with capex and net debt up INR395 crores.
Tax expense elevated at consolidated level because losses at overseas and new Indian subsidiaries get no tax credit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the demand and margin recovery narrative, but cautious on H1 FY27 margins, tariff timing and AGOA renewal. Management repeatedly hedged FY28 and FY27 guidance with geopolitical caveats and declined to factor in pending FTAs.
key_quotes: So, overall, I don't see any problem from a demand standpoint.
It looks like the worst is behind us.
Africa is not under Section 301 investigation, giving further comfort.
Certainly, there is no rebate on top of it at all for the year.

Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) 1,000-machine unit, adds about INR175 crores revenue at full capacity

growth.why: Management targets at least 15% FY27 growth (excluding U.K./EU FTA upside) backed by Karnataka and Bhopal ramp-ups adding about INR300 crores revenue, two new premium customers in India and two in Africa, and Africa target of $115-120 million; Africa's $80 million FY26 base implies a large step-up, and H1 pricing concessions and Q4 India ops growth of only 2% temper confidence.
